description: Machine-readable conventions that hold for EVERY project, whatever its stack. One file, one section per topic; a topic moves here from prose when a tool can read it. Profile-dependent values do not belong here: they live in the stack profiles (shared/profiles/*.json, and .shipwright/profiles/ for a project's own), which refine these conventions, never contradict them. Sections today: skill_authoring (the machine-readable half of docs/building-skills-plugins-agents.md). The constitution and the architecture rules are prose and stack-profile keys today and are the next candidates.

skill_authoring.description: The numeric limits and the alignment with Anthropic's 'Skill authoring best practices' (platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices, read 2026-11-15). The four rules themselves are prose and live only in docs/building-skills-plugins-agents.md, which explains and links and repeats no number here. Read by shared/scripts/tools/check_skill_authoring.py. On any conflict the Shipwright rule wins.

limits.note: name and description are the two required fields
lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens only
name and description are the two required fields; description must be non-empty

Anthropic: 'under 500 lines', so a body of this many lines or more is reported. The page names no token limit. Shipwright's own, stricter runtime-prompt size limit and its anti-ratchet baseline are enforced elsewhere (see shared/prompts/writing-plugin.md) and not repeated here
every reference file is linked from SKILL.md; a reference that links on to another reference file makes Claude preview it with head and read it incompletely

a reference file longer than this starts with a table of contents; 'starts with' is read as: within the first 'window' lines (a heading named Contents, or an in-page anchor link). The window is a judgement call, small enough that a partial read (head -100) still sees it
judgement, not countable: a description says what the skill does and when to use it, in third person. Reviewed by a person or the AI.

limits.source: Claude Code docs, UNVERIFIED: second-hand from a research report of a parallel session (2026-11-14); check code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md and context-window.md before relying on it
limits.note: if the number holds it is looser than description-max-length, which would already keep us under it
